added_lemmas.statement:
For every \(C,D\in\mathfrak S_p\), if \(\mathsf S(C)\neq\mathsf S(D)\), then
\[
\mathcal W_2(C)\not\subseteq\mathcal M(D)
\qquad\text{or}\qquad
\mathcal W_2(D)\not\subseteq\mathcal M(C).
\]
Moreover, for every \(E_0\in\mathfrak S_p\), writing \(b_j=|\Pi^{E_0}_j|\),
\[
|\mathcal W_2(E_0)|
=\sum_{j\in V}\left(b_j+\binom{b_j}{2}\right)
=\sum_{j\in V}\binom{b_j+1}{2}
\leq\binom{p+1}{3}
\leq\frac{p^2(p-1)}{2}.
\]
The bound \(\binom{p+1}{3}\) is sharp for every \(p\geq1\): equality is attained by a transitively oriented complete directed acyclic graph whose parent partitions consist entirely of singleton blocks.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Suppose first that \(\mathsf S(C)\neq\mathsf S(D)\).  By the bounded binary-star separation theorem, there are distinct states \(E,J\in\{C,D\}\), a target \(z\in V\), and a subfamily \(\mathcal A_z\subseteq\Pi^E_z\) with \(1\leq|\mathcal A_z|\leq2\) such that the corresponding covariance \(\Sigma^{\star}\) belongs to \(\mathcal M(E)\setminus\mathcal M(J)\).  By the binary-star-library definition, the same choices imply \(\Sigma^{\star}\in\mathcal W_2(E)\).  Hence, if \(E=C\), then \(\mathcal W_2(C)\not\subseteq\mathcal M(D)\), while if \(E=D\), then \(\mathcal W_2(D)\not\subseteq\mathcal M(C)\).  This proves the separating-dictionary assertion.

It remains to count the library exactly.  Fix \(E_0\in\mathfrak S_p\), and put \(b_j=|\Pi^{E_0}_j|\).  For a target \(z\) and an admissible active subfamily \(\mathcal A_z\), let \(A_z=\bigcup_{B\in\mathcal A_z}B\).  Every block in a partition is nonempty, so \(A_z\neq\varnothing\).  Also \(z\notin A_z\), because \(A_z\subseteq\operatorname{pa}_{G_{E_0}}(z)\) and an acyclic directed graph has no self-loop.  The binary-star-library formula gives
\[
\Sigma^{\star}_{kk}
=
\begin{cases}
1+|A_z|,&k=z,\\
1,&k\neq z,
\end{cases}
\qquad
\Sigma^{\star}_{zi}=\mathbf 1\{i\in A_z\}\quad(i\neq z).
\]
Consequently \(z\) is the unique index whose diagonal entry exceeds one, and, after \(z\) is recovered,
\[
A_z=\{i\in V\setminus\{z\}:\Sigma^{\star}_{zi}=1\}.
\]
Thus the covariance recovers both its target and its active union.  Finally, because the members of \(\Pi^{E_0}_z\) are pairwise disjoint nonempty atoms, equality
\[
\bigcup_{B\in\mathcal A_z}B
=
\bigcup_{B\in\mathcal A'_z}B
\]
forces \(\mathcal A_z=\mathcal A'_z\): if \(B\in\mathcal A_z\) and \(i\in B\), then the unique partition atom containing \(i\) on the right is \(B\), so \(B\in\mathcal A'_z\), and the reverse inclusion is symmetric.  Hence the map from admissible pairs \((z,\mathcal A_z)\) to binary-star covariances is injective.  There are exactly \(\binom{b_z}{1}+\binom{b_z}{2}\) admissible subfamilies at target \(z\), including zero choices when \(b_z=0\).  Summing the disjoint, injectively represented target contributions yields
\[
|\mathcal W_2(E_0)|
=\sum_{z\in V}\left(\binom{b_z}{1}+\binom{b_z}{2}\right)
=\sum_{z\in V}\left(b_z+\binom{b_z}{2}\right)
=\sum_{z\in V}\binom{b_z+1}{2}.
\]

We next prove the uniform bound.  A finite acyclic directed graph has a topological order: indeed, every nonempty induced subgraph has a source, since otherwise repeatedly following an incoming arrow in the finite vertex set would repeat a vertex and create a directed cycle; deleting a source and iterating gives the order.  Write this order as \(v_1,\ldots,v_p\), with every arrow directed from an earlier to a later vertex.  Then
\[
|\operatorname{pa}_{G_{E_0}}(v_k)|\leq k-1.
\]
Because \(\Pi^{E_0}_{v_k}\) partitions that parent set into nonempty blocks,
\[
b_{v_k}\leq|\operatorname{pa}_{G_{E_0}}(v_k)|\leq k-1.
\]
The map \(m\mapsto\binom{m+1}{2}=m(m+1)/2\) is nondecreasing on the nonnegative integers.  Therefore
\[
|\mathcal W_2(E_0)|
=\sum_{k=1}^{p}\binom{b_{v_k}+1}{2}
\leq\sum_{k=1}^{p}\binom{k}{2}
=\binom{p+1}{3},
\]
where the last equality follows by induction from Pascal's identity \(\binom{k+1}{3}=\binom{k}{3}+\binom{k}{2}\), with both sides zero at \(p=1\).  Since \(p+1\leq3p\) for \(p\geq1\),
\[
\binom{p+1}{3}
=\frac{p(p-1)(p+1)}{6}
\leq\frac{p^2(p-1)}{2},
\]
so the former coarse bound is retained as a consequence.

For sharpness, choose any ordering \(v_1,\ldots,v_p\) of \(V\), include every arrow \(v_a\to v_b\) with \(a<b\), and let every \(\Pi^{E_0}_{v_k}\) be the singleton partition of \(\{v_1,\ldots,v_{k-1}\}\).  The graph is acyclic, these are valid parent partitions, and hence the resulting state belongs to \(\mathfrak S_p\).  It satisfies \(b_{v_k}=k-1\), so the exact identity already proved gives
\[
|\mathcal W_2(E_0)|
=\sum_{k=1}^{p}\binom{k}{2}
=\binom{p+1}{3}.
\]
Thus the global bound is attained, including the case \(p=1\), when both sides are zero.
added_lemmas.justification: The pointwise separator becomes a finite universal test dictionary with an exact pre-data size and a sharp worst-case combinatorial bound.
added_lemmas.gap: BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026 decides equality using rational model constraints, whereas this proposition reduces inequality detection on the blocked class to an exactly counted finite library of binary stars.
added_lemmas.consumer: Exact-arithmetic implementations can allocate and precompute the full separating library, with the sharp worst-case size known before observing data.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The orchestrator requires a strictly stronger conclusion: exact library cardinality, the sharp bound \(\binom{p+1}{3}\), and an attaining state. Because in-place claim changes are reserved for narrowing, the proved sharp proposition replaces the obsolete coarse-bound proposition while preserving and strengthening its separation and size claims; inbound dependencies are migrated mechanically.

prose_updates.tldr: Target-local equality constraints among structural coefficients encode causal communities, but permitting singleton communities restores observational ambiguity. Every static-signature discrepancy is nevertheless exposed by a unit-noise covariance generated from at most two coefficient-one blocks at one target, with integer entries bounded by \(p\) and an exact determinant or cleared-regression value in \(\{-2,-1,1,2\}\). The resulting universal binary-star library has the exact size \(\sum_j[|\Pi^{E_0}_j|+\binom{|\Pi^{E_0}_j|}{2}]\), at most the sharp worst-case value \(\binom{p+1}{3}\). Covariance-model equality is equivalent to signature equality and to connectivity by legal singleton covered reversals, enabling exact component enumeration and a qualified fixed-\(p\) rung for generic global-BIC component recovery and simultaneous member-labelled total-effect inference.

project_justification.gap: BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026 proves identifiability only when every blocked edge-colour class is nonsingleton and leaves graphical equivalence open. Its rational constraints and the determinant machinery of SullivantTalaskaDraisma2010 and DrtonRobevaWeihs2020 do not provide a uniformly small observable witness, an exactly counted universal witness library, or a sharp worst-case library bound when singleton blocks are admitted.
project_justification.niche: The target-local blocked class has enough structure for every skeleton, collider, block-family, or unequal-family orientation mismatch to be routed to one sparse star calculation. Partition disjointness makes the star parametrization injective, while acyclicity bounds the exact library size through a topological order, and the class still contains ordinary Markov equivalence and the proper BPEC boundary as opposite special cases.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the four-case binary-star router and logarithmic numerical-height guarantee, counts its universal library exactly and obtains the sharp bound \(\binom{p+1}{3}\), lifts Chickering's disagreement-decreasing sequence to the exact legal blocked move graph, enumerates the resulting component, and establishes pointwise generic selection and effect-set inference without claiming uniformity at model intersections.

prose_updates.related_work: BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026 provides the model exemplar: its Introduction moves from equality-constrained causal coefficients to causal communities, Theorem 19 proves proper BPEC identifiability, and Question 20 isolates general edge-coloured equivalence; the present strict advance is confined to target-local blocked colours with singleton blocks and adds bounded constructive separators together with an exactly counted binary-star dictionary whose sharp worst-case size is \(\binom{p+1}{3}\). Chickering1995, Theorems 1 and 2, supplies the ordinary skeleton-collider criterion and the disagreement-decreasing covered-reversal induction; the new step is proving that equal blocked signatures force every selected move to be singleton and partition-compatible. SullivantTalaskaDraisma2010 supplies the determinant-expansion viewpoint, while DrtonRobevaWeihs2020 supplies the cleared rational-constraint analogue; both inform the certificate proof but are not claimed to be sharpened in their general graph classes. WuDrton2023 gives the nearest complete partition-restricted equivalence theorem for innovation variances, a different parameter restriction. MakamReichenbachSeigal2023 supplies the target-local pooled-regression likelihood construction. WienobstLuttermannBannachLiskiewicz2023 informs consistent-extension enumeration with background arrows. Haughton1988 informs the smooth finite-model BIC argument. NandyMaathuisRichardson2017 and StriederDrton2023 inform the simultaneous effect-set inference rung. Targeted searches through September 2026 found no paper occupying the bounded binary-star target-method pair, the exact sharp dictionary count, or the stated singleton-permitting blocked equivalence criterion.
prose_updates.interpretation: The causal target is the covariance-model equivalence component, whereas the static signature and the finite star dictionary are observable-law recovery devices whose correctness is proved rather than assumed. A signature mismatch can be rejected by searching a finite source-model library, and the exact count shows the computational certificate budget is determined by the parent-block counts. The sharp worst case occurs for a complete acyclic graph with singleton parent blocks; coarser blocks or missing arrows can only reduce the library.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: Exact-arithmetic enumeration through \(p=5\) remains a diagnostic audit of the constructive proof, not a premise of it: the all-\(p\) router, exact dictionary count, and sharp bound are established symbolically. The unresolved certificate Pareto question is whether a different universal scheme can improve on two active blocks or height \(\lceil\log_2p\rceil\) without worsening the other coordinate. The statistical rung remains restricted to a global optimizer, fixed \(p\), pointwise parameters outside the stated algebraic exceptional set, and simultaneous inference over a finite recovered component.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Population equivalence allows zero coefficients and all positive innovation variances and makes no faithfulness assumption. The bounded separator, exact sharp dictionary count, complete equivalence, and finite component enumeration hold for all \(p\) in the singleton-permitting target-local blocked class. No Pareto optimality of the two-block or height guarantees is claimed. Statistical conclusions are global-optimizer, fixed-\(p\), pointwise, and generic. Greedy GECS consistency, growing dimension, uniform inference near model intersections, cross-target edge-colour classes, constrained innovation variances, and cyclic graphs are outside scope.
